TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The document is titled "Electronic Fuel Injection" and authored by Dr. S. John Alexis (Page 1)
- A modern gasoline injection system uses pressure generated by an electric fuel pump to spray fuel into the engine intake manifold (Page 2)
- The gasoline injection system must provide the correct air-fuel mixture for specific operating conditions, using pressure instead of engine vacuum to feed fuel, making it very efficient (Page 3)
- A gasoline injection system has several advantages over a carburetor: improved atomization through pressurized fuel delivery, better fuel distribution ensuring equal vapor flow to each cylinder, and smoother idle due to more consistent fuel mixture and low-speed atomization (Page 4)
- Electronic fuel injection systems offer reduced emissions due to lean air-fuel mixtures, improved cold weather drivability through better mixture control, increased engine power from precise fuel and air flow metering, and mechanical simplicity with fewer parts compared to computer-controlled carburetors (Page 5)
- There are many types of gasoline injection systems; the two main classifications are single- or multi-point injection and indirect or direct injection (Page 6)
- Single Point Fuel Injection (TBI) has the injector located inside the throttle body, positioned above the throttle valve, spraying fuel into the air stream before it enters the inlet manifold, controlled by the ECU (Page 7)
- Multipoint Fuel Injection (MPI) involves injectors located in each branch of the inlet manifold, below the throttle valve, spraying fuel directly into each port, controlled by the ECU (Page 8)
- The Single Point Fuel Injection (TBI) system uses a single injector that serves all cylinders through the intake manifold (Page 9)
- A multi-point injection system has an injector in the port going to each cylinder, spraying gasoline into each intake port toward the intake valve, justifying the term "multipoint" (Page 10)
- An indirect injection system sprays fuel into the engine intake manifold, common in gasoline engines, while direct injection forces fuel directly into the combustion chamber, used in diesel engines (Page 13)
- Gasoline electronic Direct Injection Systems are classified as both multi-point and direct injection systems (Page 13)
- Electronic fuel injectors can withstand combustion conditions by using the fuel passing through them as a coolant (Page 12)
- A fuel system block diagram includes components such as the Fuel Supply System, Fuel Metering System, Engine, Air Supply System, Cold Start System, Control System, and Detecting System, with lines representing connections and arrows showing flow direction (Page 14)

- The document is titled "Electronic Fuel Injection" and authored by Dr. S. John Alexis (Page 1)
- A modern gasoline injection system uses pressure generated by an electric fuel pump to spray fuel into the engine intake manifold (Page 2)
- The gasoline injection system must provide the correct air-fuel mixture for specific operating conditions, using pressure instead of engine vacuum to feed fuel, making it very efficient (Page 3)
- A gasoline injection system has several advantages over a carburetor: improved atomization through pressurized fuel delivery, better fuel distribution ensuring equal vapor flow to each cylinder, and smoother idle due to more consistent fuel mixture and low-speed atomization (Page 4)
- Electronic fuel injection systems offer reduced emissions due to lean air-fuel mixtures, improved cold weather drivability through better mixture control, increased engine power from precise fuel and air flow metering, and mechanical simplicity with fewer parts compared to computer-controlled carburetors (Page 5)
- There are many types of gasoline injection systems; the two main classifications are single- or multi-point injection and indirect or direct injection (Page 6)
- Single Point Fuel Injection (TBI) has the injector located inside the throttle body, positioned above the throttle valve, spraying fuel into the air stream before it enters the inlet manifold, controlled by the ECU (Page 7)
- Multipoint Fuel Injection (MPI) involves injectors located in each branch of the inlet manifold, below the throttle valve, spraying fuel directly into each port, controlled by the ECU (Page 8)
- The Single Point Fuel Injection (TBI) system uses a single injector that serves all cylinders through the intake manifold (Page 9)
- A multi-point injection system has an injector in the port going to each cylinder, spraying gasoline into each intake port toward the intake valve, justifying the term "multipoint" (Page 10)
- An indirect injection system sprays fuel into the engine intake manifold, common in gasoline engines, while direct injection forces fuel directly into the combustion chamber, used in diesel engines (Page 13)
- Gasoline electronic Direct Injection Systems are classified as both multi-point and direct injection systems (Page 13)
- Electronic fuel injectors can withstand combustion conditions by using the fuel passing through them as a coolant (Page 12)
- A fuel system block diagram includes components such as the Fuel Supply System, Fuel Metering System, Engine, Air Supply System, Cold Start System, Control System, and Detecting System, with lines representing connections and arrows showing flow direction (Page 14)

pages.summary:
This page provides an overview of Throttle Body Injection (TBI) systems, explaining their operation and key components. It describes how TBI uses one or two injectors to spray fuel into the top of the throttle body air horn, where it mixes with air before being drawn into the engine. The text highlights that the fuel pressure regulator is spring-loaded and integrated into the housing, and notes that this system operates continuously while the engine is running, also known as a Continuous Injection System (CIS). Two images are included: a larger, angled view of a TBI unit and a smaller, top-down view showing its internal structure.

**Text Evidence:**
- Throttle Body Injection uses one or two injectors.
- Injectors (pulse) spray fuel into the top of the throttle body air horn.
- Atomized fuel mixes with air and is drawn into the engine.
- The fuel pressure regulator is spring loaded and part of the housing.
- Fuel is injected whenever the engine is running, also called CIS: Continuous Injection System.
